- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for risk premium or reversal.
- Model consistently overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5 → -0.5 → 0.5), model often misjudges direction; align forecast to sentiment median rather than peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days of forecast to capture momentum.
